To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the non-histone proteins of chicken liver nuclei are composed of several immunologically related proteins, which can be separated by chromatography on DEAE-Sephacel and DNA-affinity chromatograpy.

1) chicken liver nuclei contain a DNA-binding immunoreac- tive protein (CS), representing 5% of total nuclear DNA, 2) this DNA-binding immunoreactiv protein is a transcription inhibitor in the in vitro transcription system, 3) this protein is not a histone.
the CS contains two proteins (Mr 35 and 57 kD) that are immunologically related to non-histone proteins in chromatin, and that they inhibit in vitro transcription of DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of a protein component of chicken liver chromatin, which is capable of inhibiting the in vitro transcription.
the identification of the protein components of chicken liver chromatin which are involved in the regulation of gene expression.
the isolation of the DNA-binding protein from chicken liver nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA-binding proteins of the chromatin are involved in the regulation of transcription.
the DNA-binding proteins in the CS fraction are non-histone proteins and that they may play a role in regulating the in vitro transcription.
this DNA-binding protein is a transcription factor, and that the transcription factor is not a histone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CS is a specific fraction of non-histonic proteins, which is capable of inhibiting transcription in vitro.
the DNA-binding component is a transcription inhibitor.
this protein fraction (CS) represents the non-histone chromosomal protein (NCP) which is involved in the regulation of transcription of the chromatin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CS fraction contains a protein which inhibits in vitro transcription of DNA and which is recognized by anti-chromatin sera.
this DNA-binding protein is a transcriptional repressor.
we have identified a DNA-binding protein that inhibits transcription in vitro.
